content_of_post_to_comment: A storm is raging over on the Twitter app, over the fact that Claude will break off communication if you use abusive language towards it. Does building an assistant that behaves this way mean that Anthropic is blameworthy? The two camps seem to be: 1) Anthropic is not blameworthy because abusing an assistant is bad behaviour, even if the assistant is a machine 2) Anthropic is blameworthy because machines are tools, and it's no one else's business how a user employs tools This is interesting because it's two ethical theories at war. 1) is Aristotelian: we judge behaviour based on what it says about the person and the habits it is likely to engender 2) is classically liberal: we must disavow judgment on private behaviour because accounts of the good life differ Intellectually, I find myself in sympathy with both sides. But emotionally, I'm 1) all the way: cursing at Claude and being abusive to Claude in conversation is abhorrent to me, because it suggests to me what kind of person the abuser is, or is becoming.
